messages:
Maya D.: Hey team — putting up suggested microcopy for the rollback flow where we purge KV cache as part of a model rollback. Trying three tones, and a short tooltip for the cache impact. PTAL and leave quick thumbs or short edits.

Maya D.: Confirmation dialog (Option A — direct):
```
Title: Roll back to previous version?
Body: Rolling back will replace the current model and purge its KV cache. This may temporarily increase latency for recent sessions. Are you sure you want to continue?
Primary CTA: Roll back and purge cache
Secondary CTA: Cancel
```

Maya D.: Confirmation dialog (Option B — reassuring):
```
Title: Confirm rollback and cache reset
Body: Well restore the previous model version. To ensure correctness, the models KV cache will be cleared, which can briefly slow responses until the cache warms up.
Primary CTA: Yes, roll back
Secondary CTA: No, keep current
```

Maya D.: Tooltip for the KV cache label (short): `Clearing the KV cache removes recent context used to speed responses.`

Sam P.: +1 on Option B tone, feels less scary. Can we avoid jargon like "KV" in the primary dialog? Non-technical PMs will read this. Maybe say "context cache (used to speed up replies)" once and then use "cache" after.

Lee (a11y): Agree re: expand KV to "context cache" the first time. Also, for screen readers we should include the consequence in the dialog role text: e.g., `dialog, Rollback will clear the context cache and may increase latency briefly.` Keep the primary CTA text concise (no more than ~30 chars) and avoid punctuation that confuses voice controls.

Jonah R.: UX nit: our button max width is 220px in the modal so long labels wrap. Can we get proposed exact strings for CTAs to test? Also need the i18n keys. For Option B CTAs I'd suggest: `Yes, roll back` (primary) and `Cancel` (secondary). Both short.

Ava - Eng: Implementation note: when we purge cache we emit event `cache.purged` and start a background warmup. If copy mentions "briefly slow responses" we should limit to "may experience slightly higher latency for a few minutes" so it's factual. Also ask localization team about the word "warm up" — some langs translate oddly.

Maya D.: Updated CTA strings for Option B per Jonah: `Yes, roll back` / `Cancel`. Updated body copy to: "We'll restore the previous model version. The context cache will be cleared; you may see slightly higher latency for a few minutes while the cache warms up."

Maya D.: Tooltip (final): `Context cache: temporary data that speeds up recent requests. Clearing it may slow responses until it's rebuilt.`

Lee (a11y): For the tooltip, ensure its accessible: use an `aria-describedby` target and make the tooltip text available to screen readers (not just hover). Also prefer full sentences for SR clarity.

Sam P.: One more ask: can we add a one-line inline help under the rollback toggle in the console: `Rolling back clears recent cache to ensure consistency.` Short and scannable.

Jonah R.: Sounds good. Ill mock the modal with these strings and test wrapping in localized mockups. ETA EOD.

Ava - Eng: FYI, backend already supports emitting duration in telemetry of how long the cache takes to rewarm — we can show a short toast: `Cache warming in progress — performance may be degraded for ~5–10 min.` Is that okay copy-wise?

Maya D.: I like that — non-technical and sets expectations. Suggested toast: `Cache warming in progress. Responses may be slower for a few minutes.`

Lee (a11y): For the toast, ensure it's announced by SR politely (role=alert) but not overly verbose. Keep it under ~80 characters. The Maya toast looks good.

DesignBot: Reminder: strings longer than 120 chars flagged for translation review. Current body copy length check: OK.

Sam P.: Great, thanks everyone. Jonah, ping here when you have the mock so we can quick-approve and pass to localization. :thumbsup:
